_doc: The AUTHORED half of the terrain for epoch e1834_harbor_cut. generators/terrain_gen.py reads this plus river.geojson, hydrology.geojson, shoreline.geojson and branches.geojson and writes heightfield.json + heightfield.bin + the terrain GLBs. Loading a vector file does not put its features in the ground: this spec names the ones the field reads, by id. Every elevation here traces to a numbered zone in docs/research/01-terrain-hydrology.md; nothing is invented to make the ground interesting. Elevations are in FEET above the summer-1835 lake and river water surface (the internal datum, data/datum.json) and are converted to metres at generation.
scope: The forks AND the harbour: the Chicago River from the North and South Branches at Wolf Point east down the main stem, through the 1834 cut, past the sand bar and the decaying old southward channel, to open Lake Michigan — and, since T-1123, the North Branch above the forks to the north line of Wright's survey. Land is the three divisions the river separates, the Fort Dearborn reservation, the lakeshore sand-ridge belt east of State Street, the North Division ground Kinzie's Addition is platted on, and the bar itself.
critical_caveat: No contour survey of the 1835 town site exists. The earliest systematic levels are the 1850s street-grade and Chesbrough sewerage surveys. Every land elevation below is a period narrative statement in feet, back-calculated from grade-raising records, or inferred from geology — so NO land elevation in this spec is better than 'inferred', and the generator refuses to emit a 'documented' confidence for any land vertex. The one documented surface is the water: the pre-reversal river was sluggish and outward-flowing with a near-zero surface gradient, standing at lake level through the whole downtown reach.

grid.note: 2405 x 4920 m, 2.5 m cells (8.2 ft — inside the dossier's 5-10 ft), quantised at 5 mm, which is 1/15 of the 0.25 ft the dossier asks for. 963 x 1969 = 1 896 147 samples, 3.79 MB. Row 0 is the SOUTH edge. This box is the union of three extensions that were open at once and could not be merged: T-0464 carried the south wall from Madison Street to Twenty-Second (N -530 -> -3800), T-1123 carried the north wall from the North Branch's old traced end to the north line of Wright's survey (N +400 -> +1120), and T-1416 carried the west wall from the forks trace's own reading window to the easting T-1415 derived (E -320 -> -705). Two heightfields cannot be merged, so the field below is regenerated once against all four walls rather than reconciled.

box_derivation._doc: Why these four numbers, each from evidence rather than from a round figure.
box_derivation.e_max: +1700. The easternmost thing this scene contains is the north pier's 1835 head at about E +1510 (root E +1243.5 / N +311.9, bearing 103.36 deg, 900 ft adopted — docs/RESEARCH/north_pier.md sections 2 and 4), with a +/-30 m band on the length. The easternmost traced LAND is the sand bar's east edge at E +1497.5, and the traced water stops at E +1573.6, which is the edge of the tracing window and not a shore. +1700 clears the pier head by 190 m and its error bar by 160 m, clears the traced window by 126 m so the whole traced water body is inside the box, and stands 203 m (665 ft) off the bar — inside dossier zone 30's 600-1000 ft, where the lake reaches about -10 ft. It is deliberately NOT taken from the drafted pier ends at E +1588.8: Wright draws both piers at about 1165 ft, longer than the north pier was in 1834 and longer than the south pier ever was before 1837, so the drafted extent is an AUTHORISATION and not a length at any date this project models.
box_derivation.e_min:
-705, AND IT IS THE LAST WALL OF THIS BOX TO BE DERIVED. Until T-1415 it was -320: the forks trace's own western window — where tools/trace_river.py stopped reading — adopted rather than argued, which was defensible while nothing in the town stood west of it and stopped being defensible when 35 West Division placements were held for want of ground. The successor stands on the same three tests the other three walls do, and T-1416 is the run that spent the Blender bake `grid` costs and built the field to it.
CONTAINS. data/reconstruction/1835_phase2_west_wolf_point_approaches.json holds 35 of its 55 West Division placements behind its own `terrain_and_hydrology_gate`, and the westernmost is west_rec_055 at E -668.0. THE WALL IS NOT DERIVED FROM THAT CENTRE: a 22 x 36 ft footprint rotated -2 degrees reaches 3.54 m west of it, to E -671.54, and a roof is contained when all of it is — generate_west_infill.py's own validator tests the whole footprint for exactly this reason. -705 clears that edge by 33.46 m.
THE ERROR BAR, AND WHY THE RECIPE'S ROUND FIGURE FAILS IT. The memo asks for E -700, and -700 is a round number rather than a measurement. The West Division centres are dealt against a street grid fitted to the Wright 1834 sheet, so the bar is the georeference's own: data/datum.json records RMS 17.5 m and a MAXIMUM residual of 32.7 m, and a wall clears ONE point — the westernmost roof — so it is owed the maximum and not the mean. -700 clears the footprint by 28.46 m and stands 4.24 m SHORT of the worst residual; -705 clears it by 0.76 m. Five metres and two columns of field buy that back.
LATTICE. -705 is 282 cells of 2.5 m west of the origin, so it lands on the sampling lattice the field already carries: 154 columns are ADDED and no committed sample moves. tools/measure_west_of_box.mjs derives all three figures rather than asserting them, and tools/check.sh holds data/terrain/west_of_box_reading.json against a re-derivation, so the wall moves when a placement moves rather than when somebody remembers.
WHAT THE MOVE BROUGHT INSIDE, and the one thing it obliged. Three platted-only street lines (school_section_line_1, des_plaines_school_section, jefferson_school_section) come onto modelled ground; the 4 797.5 m of one-way boundary scarp the old wall stood as goes with it; and the North Branch's traced terminus at (E -481.31, N +1079.21) — the top edge of Wright's sheet, not the end of a river — comes inside the box, 40.79 m short of the north wall. A river that stops in the middle of the modelled ground is a defect, so `northern_branch` carries the channel from that edge to the wall between the two banks `trace_carries` already carries there. Nine platted-only lines in Wabansia and the School Section still stand west of the wall, none of them drawn; they are recorded in west_of_box_reading.json § streets.
box_derivation.n_min:
-3800. Was -530, and -530 was the PLAT's south line: Madison Street, where T-0219 stopped because the plat stopped. This box is no longer only the plat's. T-0464 carries it south far enough to CONTAIN the ground the 1812 and 1880s scene tickets stand on — the evacuation corridor and the Prairie Avenue district, both of them between Twelfth Street and Twenty-Second — so the bound is set on Twenty-Second Street (Cermak Road) and derived from the PLSS rather than from a round figure.
THE DERIVATION. Two committed section corners fix the mile. G1 of data/traces/gcp/wright_1834_gcps.json is State & Madison, the corner of sections 9/10/15/16, at local N -525.27. S-SE of data/traces/gcp/wright_1834_nara_hup_section_corners.json is State & Roosevelt — Twelfth Street — the corner of sections 15/16/21/22, at local N -2149.40. Those are the north and south lines of the School Section, one statute mile apart, and Twenty-Second Street is the next mile line south: the south line of sections 21/22. One statute mile (1609.344 m) below S-SE puts it at local N -3758.74.
THE BUFFER, MEASURED. -3800 stands 41.3 m south of that line. The uncertainty it has to clear is stated by the control itself: the square those OSM crossings make measures 1620.09 to 1624.23 m against the mile, a mean 12.73 m long, because Halsted and Twelfth were both widened after 1834 and a one-sided widening moves a centreline. Carry that measured spacing instead of the statute mile and Twenty-Second falls at N -3773.5; -3800 clears that reading too, by 26.5 m, and clears the picking spread (16.95 m at Halsted & Roosevelt) as well. So the street is inside the box on either derivation, which is what 'through Cermak' has to mean. -3800 also lands on the existing 2.5 m lattice (1308 rows below -530), so no sample the field already carried moves.
WHAT IS DOWN THERE, AND IT IS NOT RECONSTRUCTION. Nothing in this corpus states ground south of Twelfth Street. The terrain dossier's own scope is 'south to about Van Buren/Madison'; its one southern statement is zone 3, the lakeshore sand-ridge belt, given as Chicago Ave to 12th St; Wright's sheet ends there; and both traced lines — the South Branch in branches.geojson and south_shore_harbor_reach — stop within 15 m of the same section line. So the 1650 m below it was FRAME and not reconstruction, and evidence_limit still marks every vertex there conjectural. What is no longer frame is the WATER. T-0465 split into the pieces that carry the river and the shore down into it, and two have landed off one acquired sheet, REES & RUCKER 1849: T-1150 traced the South Branch below Twelfth Street and deleted `southern_branch`, and T-1151 traced the pre-fill lake shore and deleted `southern_lake.beyond_the_trace`. Neither reach is held on an easting any more, and no code reads one. The LAND down here is still frame.
box_derivation.n_max: +1120, AND IT IS THE TRACE THAT SETS IT, as it set +400 before. The old number was capped by "the North Branch's traced water ends at N +401.6", and that cap is spent: branches.geojson carries the North Branch and both its banks from the forks to the north line of Wright's survey — water to local N +1079.21, west bank +1075.48, east bank +1076.41 — and shoreline.geojson carries the north shore and the lake margin north of the harbour to N +1117.30, with the lake water polygon reaching +1121.00. +1120 is held to the same three tests the other three walls are. It clears the northernmost traced water by 1.0 m, so the whole traced body is inside the box as e_max requires of the lake. It clears Wolcott Street's north end at N +1029.71 — the northernmost committed street in data/streets/1835.json — by 90 m, and Superior Street, Kinzie's Addition's northernmost east-west line, at +1017.11 by 103 m. And it lands on the existing 2.5 m lattice, at row 660 counted from n_min, so every sample the field already carries keeps its own position and only its row index moves, which is the property the southern extension was careful to keep. WHAT IT COST, stated because T-1067 filed this as a separate piece of work: 809 x 373 = 301 757 samples become 809 x 661 = 534 749, a 77 % larger field and 1.02 MB of heightfield.bin against 590 KB, plus the ground mesh, the publish budget and the draw-call and triangle gates. WHAT THE NORTH WALL ACTUALLY CUTS, which is not what the trace's northern extents suggest: the North Branch runs north-WEST out of the forks and crosses this box's own west wall at about N +720, so above that row the branch is outside the box altogether and the north wall at +1120 stands on North Division land from E -320 east to the lake shore at about E +1225, and on lake beyond it. The 41 m between the branch's traced wash (+1079.21) and this wall is 166 m west of the box and never reaches the field. See `northern_lake` for the one thing the extension did break.
box_derivation.what_this_truncates: The bar's southern hook below N -400 (34 m of a 660 m island) and the lake shore north of N +400. North of that wall stands the whole of Kinzie's Addition. 47 of the 49 platted, unopened street records in data/streets/1835.json stand off the modelled ground and draw nothing — renderers/web/js/streets.js compiles no ribbon for a record with track_width_m 0 — and the one DRAWN ribbon that leaves the box, Wolcott Street, runs 629.72 m of its 921.73 m on the renderer's fallback constant rather than on a measurement. tools/measure_north_of_box.mjs measures it, data/terrain/north_of_box_reading.json is the committed reading, and tools/check.sh holds the two against each other. The old southward channel's natural outlet at about Madison Street (local N -525) is now INSIDE the box, which is the second thing the southern extension buys. Below N -530 the South Branch and the lake shore both continue in branches.geojson, shoreline.geojson and data/traces/vectors/wright_1834_east.json as evidence; none of it is modelled ground.  AND SOUTH OF MADISON IT NOW TRUNCATES NOTHING ANY SOURCE HERE DESCRIBES (T-0464): the wall stands on Twenty-Second Street, a mile and a half below the last thing this corpus says about ground. What is truncated there is the EVIDENCE and not the ground, which is why every vertex below N -2149.4 is written conjectural rather than inferred — see `evidence_limit`.

vertical.datum: Z = 0.0 ft at the summer-1835 lake and river water surface
vertical.exaggeration_note: 1.0 and it stays 1.0 in the data. Total natural relief on land inside this box is under 12 ft, which is what the dossier's 'under fifteen feet across the whole modeled area' allows. A vertical-exaggeration control may exist in a renderer, labelled, defaulting off — see docs/LIBERTIES.md L3.

water.note: Flat. Pre-reversal flow was sluggish and outward into the lake with a near-zero surface gradient, so the water surface is effectively at lake level throughout the downtown reach; the river gradient is treated as zero. The lake is the same surface: the river stood at lake level, which is why a bar across its mouth could close it.
water.mesh_note: The water surface is the plane Z = 0 by the definition of this project's vertical datum, and terrain_gen.py emits it at a literal zero rather than reading this figure. dossier_zone is a record label for the panel, not a build input.

water_polygons.note: The forks: main stem, North Branch and South Branch. Traced from Wright 1834 by tools/trace_river.py.

The harbour reach from the east edge of the forks window to the lake: the main stem, the 1834 cut between its piers, the old southward channel behind the bar, and the lake margin. Interior ring 1 is the SAND BAR, which is land the water goes round — the reason the field has to understand islands and not only banks. Traced by tools/trace_shoreline.py; the two windows overlap between E +314 and E +390 and agree there to 0.1-5.7 m.

The South Branch below the forks window: from that window's own south edge (map row 2372, a declared splice rather than a tolerance — see tools/trace_south_branch.py) down through the School Section. Only its reach above N -530 is inside this box. Traced from Wright 1834 by tools/trace_south_branch.py.

The North Branch above the forks window: from that window's own north edge (BPL master row 1252, a declared splice rather than a tolerance — see docs/RESEARCH/north_branch_wabansia.md) up to the north line Wright ruled across the top of his sheet. It abuts river.geojson and moves no vertex of it. SINCE T-1416 THE WHOLE REACH IS INSIDE THE BOX: the west wall stood at E -320 and cut the branch off where it crosses that easting at about N +700, so the field carried roughly 320 m of channel above the forks and nothing beyond; the wall is at E -705 now and the branch's westmost traced vertex (E -502.39, N +866.46) stands 203 m inside it. The polygon's northern edge at N +1079.21 is the edge of a survey and not the end of a river — its own provenance says so — and it used to lie outside the box, so nothing here had to answer for it. It lies inside now, 40.79 m short of the north wall, and `northern_branch` is the answer.

The South Branch from Twelfth Street to the box floor, traced from REES & RUCKER 1849 by tools/trace_south_branch_rees_1849.py. THIS ENTRY REPLACES THE `southern_branch` RULE, which held a 45.3 m channel at a constant easting from N -2110 due south to the box wall because no sheet in the corpus reached past the School Section's south line. It is a trace and not a rule: the branch bends east to E +567 about Sixteenth Street and then swings south-west toward the portage, and by the box floor its centre stands 521 m west of where the held easting put it. The window's north edge is the declared row N -2110.0 -- the row the held rule carried from, and the last row Wright's trace draws two banks on rather than its closing hook -- so the two windows abut on a row both of them name, the same construction as the splice at map row 2372. Its south edge is 40 m PAST the box floor so that both perpendicular offsets cross the wall. Every vertex is INFERRED, and every vertex is also below `evidence_limit`, which writes it conjectural: the field carries the more conservative of the two.

splices.note: The forks window and the North Branch window are declared to ABUT on BPL master row 1252 — a splice and not a tolerance, so neither polygon moves a vertex of the other. As RINGS they do not quite close over each other: each ends in its own slanted chord across the channel, the forks at (E -214.7, N +401.38) to (-128.8, +403.15) and the branch at (-219.6, +402.0) through (-170.7, +403.01) to (-144.2, +403.56), and the lens between the two chords belongs to neither. At the one sampled row inside it, N +402.5, the forks ring covers E -160.3 to -128.6 and the branch ring E -219.7 to -195.4, leaving 35 m of mid-channel dry: a bar 2.5 m wide and 1.0 m high standing across the North Branch, and a sixth four-connected piece of land in a field that has four. Spanned from the BANKS instead — the two runs that meet on each side, each contributing the vertex nearest the band — which is where the trace actually speaks. The hull is E -219.59 to -128.81, 90.8 m against 86.0 m of traced channel at N +400 and 75.8 m at +405, so it is the wider of the two readings across one row and cannot remove a cell either ring claims.

The same seam at the other end, and the same bar: 12 cells of dry ground at E +5 to +32.5 on row N -405, standing across the South Branch since T-0219 spliced these two windows together. It went unseen because nothing looked — the field's dry land was counted in four connected pieces and a twelve-cell bar is not one of them at the threshold that count uses. T-1123 built the northern twin of it and found both. The geometry is the mirror image: the forks ring closes on the chord (E +35.9, N -404.33) to (-8.1, -405.24) and the South Branch ring opens on (-8.1, -405.97) to (+35.9, -405.06). The bank hull here is E -8.08 to +35.92, 44.0 m, which is the traced channel width at N -402.5 (43.9 m) and at N -407.5 (43.9 m) to a decimetre — the two windows agree at this splice and only the sampling fell between them.

open_lake.rule: east of the easternmost traced water in each row, water continues
open_lake.note: The harbour-reach polygon's EASTERN boundary is the tracing window, not a shore (its own provenance says so). Beyond it Wright's sheet is still lake wash. Treating that ground as LAND would invent a headland out in the lake — a false coast is the single largest claim available in this quadrant — so it is declared water instead. Stated as a rule against the trace rather than as a hand-drawn polygon, so it cannot drift if the trace is ever refit: in each row, everything east of the easternmost traced water cell is lake. The guard keeps the rule where the argument for it holds: it must stand east of anything that could let a row's easternmost traced water fall WEST of real land. It was +1400 while the box stopped at N -400, on the ground that the easternmost traced LAND is the sand bar at E +1497.5 and every row's traced water reaches further east than +1400. The southern extension (T-0219) breaks the second half of that: below about N -440 the harbour trace's east edge falls back to E +1235 to +1310, no row there reaches +1400, the rule did not fire, and 460 m of Lake Michigan came out as dry land walled off from the old southward channel by a 4.8 m cliff. The guard is therefore +1200, which is east of every traced shore in the box except the harbour mouth and the bar — and the bar is an island ring, subtracted after this rule rather than exposed to it. Lowering it changes NO row that already had traced water east of +1400, because the rule fills east of the row's EASTERNMOST traced water and a lower guard cannot move that maximum; it is a strict addition to the rows the old guard silenced, and the regenerated field proves it (the 259 689 samples of the old box come back with 181 cells changed, all of them in the West Division's south-west corner and all by one 5 mm quantisation step). This boundary is a RULE and not a waterline: generators/terrain_gen.py never measures shore distance to it, so no bank is raised along it. The bed under it is dossier zone 30, which the dossier itself tags conjectural.

southern_lake.rule: south of N -400, east of the row's easternmost crossing of the traced lake shore, water continues
southern_lake.note:
open_lake's companion, and it exists because open_lake's per-row test measures from the traced WATER WASH. That test holds north of N -400, where the harbour trace covers a continuous lake margin and every row's wash reaches past the guard. South of it the wash is patches — the old southward channel here, a lobe of lake there — and the ground BETWEEN two patches is not east of the easternmost one, so it stood as land: 9.4 ft of South Division sand-ridge crest on a plateau at E +1240 to +1310 between N -405 and -480, walled off from the channel beside it by a 4.8 m cliff, which is a headland invented in Lake Michigan and the largest false claim available in this quadrant. What the trace DOES carry south of N -400 is the SHORE: south_shore_harbor_reach is the east edge of Fractional Section 15, a surveyed line, and it runs unbroken to the foot of the sheet. A fractional section is fractional because the lake takes the rest of it, so east of that line there is water, and the rule is stated on it. It is a RULE and not a waterline: terrain_gen.py measures shore distance to the run itself, which is a traced bank, so the bank face south of the fort is raised off the survey line and not off this rule. Islands are subtracted after it, so the sand bar's southern hook (traced to N -436) is unaffected. Applied south of N -400 and no further north because every row above that line is already covered by open_lake and this rule must not move a sample the field has already committed — the regenerated field is checked against the old one and the whole 259 689-sample overlap comes back with 181 cells changed, all in the West Division's south-west corner and all by one 5 mm step.
THE RULE NOW REACHES THE BOX FLOOR ON A TRACE, NOT ON A HELD EASTING (T-1151). Until this ticket the block carried `beyond_the_trace`: south of south_shore_harbor_reach's last vertex at N -2159.9 every row's edge was -inf, the rule could not fire, and 355 x 1640 m of Lake Michigan came out as dry land — so the edge was HELD at that vertex's easting, E +1347.4, for the whole 1 640 m to the floor. It was conjectural and it was the lake's half of L239. REES & RUCKER 1849 draws the pre-fill shore beside this reach; lake_shore_below_twelfth.geojson traces it (tools/trace_lake_shore_rees_1849.py) and the run is named above, so the ordinary per-row interpolation carries the rule to the floor and there is no held easting and no code behind one. The shore falls away SOUTH-EAST — E +1298.9 at the splice to E +1689.6 at the floor, 390 m of easting the held value denied — and at the floor it stands the water 342 m east of where the held easting stood it. TWO THINGS THE TRACE DOES NOT CLAIM. The sheet is fourteen years late and on a SHORE that is not neutral: the piers starved this coast of littoral drift and it eroded westward, so the traced line is a LOWER BOUND on the 1835 shore's easting, measured at 134 m of offset against Wright at N -1300 tapering to 50 m at N -2000 against about 107 m of erosion documented in docs/research/01-terrain-hydrology.md sec 4. And the two runs DISAGREE BY 49 M ON THE ROW THEY ABUT: Wright's edge at N -2159.9 is E +1347.5, this sheet's is E +1298.9. The step is left in the field rather than blended out, because a blend would be geometry from neither survey. See the geojson's `measured` block and L239.

northern_lake.rule: north of N +1112.5, east of the row's easternmost crossing of the traced lake shore, water continues
northern_lake.note: southern_lake's sentence at the other end of the same trace, and it exists for the identical reason: open_lake's per-row test measures from the traced WATER WASH, and at the very top of the harbour-reach polygon that wash frays. Its north edge runs (E +1288.1, N +1120.11) -> (+1311.2, +1114.79) -> (+1327.2, +1118.02) -> (+1344.0, +1113.3): two lobes with a notch between them, so at N +1117.5 the traced water reads as E +1222.0 to +1299.4 and again +1324.6 to +1329.1, and the 25 m between them is not east of the row's easternmost water. It stood as LAND — one cell of row, 8.2 ft of North Division sand-ridge crest standing in Lake Michigan a hundred metres off the beach, between lake floor at -1.71 m to its south and -1.73 m to its north. A causeway invented out of the top edge of a sheet. What the trace DOES carry up there is the SHORE: north_shore_harbor_reach runs unbroken to N +1117.30, so east of it there is water, and the rule is stated on that instead. Applied north of +1112.5 — the last row at which the polygon's north edge is a single unbroken span — and no further south, because every row below it is already covered by open_lake and this rule must not move a sample the field has already committed. It is a RULE and not a waterline: terrain_gen.py measures shore distance to the run itself, which is a traced bank. Above N +1117.30 the run has ended and this rule is silent; the box's last row is covered by open_lake, whose test the polygon's own north tip satisfies there.

northern_branch.rule: north of N +1079.21, between the row's crossings of the North Branch's two carried bank runs, water continues to the box wall
northern_branch.note: `northern_lake`'s sentence said about a river instead of a lake, and it exists for the reason that one does: a tracing window's top edge is not the end of the thing it draws. north_branch_wabansia's polygon closes on the line Wright ruled across the top of his sheet, at N +1079.21. While the box's west wall stood at E -320 that edge was 160 m outside it and nothing had to answer for it; T-1416 carried the wall to E -705 and brought it inside, 40.79 m short of the north wall, where it would have stood as a plug of dry West Division prairie across the head of a channel whose two banks the spec already carries to the wall (`trace_carries`, both runs, to N +1120). A river that dead-ends in the middle of the modelled ground is the land half of the same fault `southern_lake` and `northern_lake` were written against, and it is worse than theirs: theirs invented a coast, this one would dam a river 40 m from the wall a visitor can walk to. Stated PER ROW from the two carried BANKS rather than as a hand-drawn extension of the ring, so it cannot drift away from the trace it extends — and the carries run at each tip's own easting, so the channel it fills is 45.39 m wide, against 45.4 m of traced channel on the polygon's own last row. Applied north of N +1079.21 and no further south, because every row below it is already covered by the polygon and this rule must not move a sample the field has already committed. Water is written conjectural everywhere in this field, so no vertex of it claims more than a continuation is worth.

trace_carries.note: The North Branch's west bank, from its last traced vertex at (E -486.87, N +1075.48) north to the box wall. Both bank carries are OUTSIDE the box in the east-west sense — the branch has crossed the west wall 350 m further south — and they are declared because the waterline is a distance field: without them the ground in the box's north-west corner measures its distance inland from the run's last VERTEX rather than from a bank that keeps going, which is 7.6 m of error at E -320 and about two quantisation steps of ground height. Small, real, and cheaper to state than to re-derive.
The North Branch's east bank, from (E -441.48, N +1076.41) to the wall. This is the bank Kinzie's Addition's water lots front on; the note on the west bank above covers why it is carried.

The lake shore north of the harbour, from (E +1221.8, N +1117.30) to the wall — 2.7 m, and the reason it matters is out of all proportion to its length: `northern_lake` reads this run PER ROW, so the two rows above its last vertex had no shore to measure from and the rule fell silent on exactly the row where the traced wash frays. Carried at its own easting, which is what the last 11 m of the run does anyway (E +1220.5 at N +1106.4 to +1221.8 at +1117.3).

shore_runs.note: The forks window's south bank, E +36 to +390.
The same bank picked up at E +314 and carried east: main stem, the Fort Dearborn reservation's shore, and the west bank of the old southward channel. 2 466 m.

The pre-fill lake shore picked up where south_shore_harbor_reach stops at N -2159.9 and carried to the box floor: 1 640 m off REES & RUCKER 1849, the one sheet in this corpus that reaches Cermak Road. The two runs abut on that declared row and do not agree on it — 49 m, which is this shore's documented post-pier erosion and not a fit failure. INFERRED, and below `evidence_limit` besides, so the field writes it conjectural.

North bank of the main stem, the pier's inner face as drafted through the cut, and the lake shore north of the harbour. 1 568 m. docs/RESEARCH/north_pier.md notes this run is good for the pier's ROOT (its vertex at E +1234.9 / N +314.7 sits 7 m from the raster reading) and wanders north of E +1250 where the channel wash merges with the lake wash; that stretch is a shore reading of a merged envelope and carries the shoreline trace's own +/-20 m and then some.

shore_runs_note: These runs, plus the island rings, ARE the waterline. Distance is never measured to the water polygons' own boundaries, because those close across the tracing windows and a window edge is where the tracing stopped, not a bank: measuring to one would raise a bank across open water at E +314, E +390 and out in the lake.
